name: Rani-ki-Vav (The Queen's Stepwell) at Patan
description: Rani-ki-Vav on the banks of Saraswati river was built as a memorial to King Bhimdev I by his widowed queen Udayamati. Designed as an inverted temple highlighting the sanctity of water with seven subterranean levels of carved sculptural panels.
significance: Masterpiece of subterranean water architecture with over 500 principal sculptures.

name: Group of Monuments at Pattadakal
description: Pattadakal represents the high point of an eclectic art which in the 7th and 8th centuries achieved a harmonious blend of architectural forms from northern and southern India.
significance: Holy coronation site of the Badami Chalukya kings featuring the monumental Virupaksha Temple.

name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya
description: The Mahabodhi Temple Complex is one of the four holy sites related to the life of the Lord Buddha, marking the location where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment beneath the sacred Bodhi Tree.
significance: Supreme pilgrimage site of Buddhism worldwide, one of the earliest surviving brick temples in India.

name: Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara
architecture: Ancient Monastic Stupa and Vihara Architecture
description: Nalanda was an ancient monastic-scholastic university comprising stupas, shrines, viharas, and important artworks in stucco, stone and metal, attracting scholars from across Asia.
significance: The most ancient university of the Indian subcontinent.

name: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple
description: Built of lightweight floating bricks and carved sandstone with intricate bracket figures of dancing damsels and musicians carved out of black basalt rock.
significance: Celebrated for its earthquake-resistant sandbox technology and porous floating bricks.

name: Dholavira: a Harappan City
description: Dholavira is an ancient fortified city of the Harappan civilization on Khadir Bet island in the Great Rann of Kutch, known for its extraordinary water conservation reservoirs.
significance: One of the best preserved urban settlements of the South Asian Bronze Age.

name: Taj Mahal
description: An immense mausoleum of white marble built in Agra by order of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his favourite wife Mumtaz Mahal.
significance: The jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage.
